So ive done some poking around the internet and I think I can expand on this a little. As used in the series, the wind in the barley seems more of an up beat tavern song, while the traditional irish balad ''The Wind that Shakes the Barley'' is anything but upbeat. There is however a song in the Two Rivers called ''The Wind that Shakes the Willow. ''

"My love is gone, carried away by the wind that shakes the Willow. And all the land is beaten hard by the wind that shakes the Willow. But I hold her close to me In heart and dearest memory and with her strength to steal my soul, Her love to warm my heartstrings, I will stand where we once sang, Though cold wind shakes the Willow."{{Ref/book|1|17}}

This is also the song Thom plays during the rescue of Moiraine, and It's lyrics are very similar to [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wind_That_Shakes_the_Barley#Lyrics The Wind that Shakes the Barley]
